inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to finish renegotiating the 2009 agreement, threatening an indefinite nationwide strike if it does not. University shutdowns would punish students and families most of all, while exposing the cost of allowing a long-delayed dispute to drag on. The government should settle its obligations responsibly—but union leaders should also remember that students’ education must not become a bargaining chip.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU’s one-month ultimatum over the 2009 agreement is another warning that students and families are being made to bear the cost of a dispute between government and union leaders. The government should meet its obligations, but it must also uphold order and insist that education is not held hostage by threats of an indefinite nationwide strike. A responsible settlement matters; so does putting students’ future ahead of political pressure.
